candidates.name: David Crowley
candidates.background: Milwaukee County Executive since 2020, the first Black person and youngest ever elected to the office. Previously served in the Wisconsin State Assembly (2017-2020). Won the Aug 11 Democratic primary in a photo finish over state Rep. Francesca Hong; endorsed by Gov. Tony Evers.

cost.label: Badger Basics plan: $15 minimum wage now and $20 by 2030, cap child-care costs at 7% of income, energy rebates (campaign site)

health.label: Expand BadgerCare with sliding-scale income-based premiums, a public-option approach (campaign site)

housing.label: Mixed tools: zoning flexibility for duplexes/fourplexes AND down-payment assistance, eviction prevention, Housing First (campaign site)

immigration.label: Publicly objected to ICE arrests at the Milwaukee County courthouse: they 'undermine public trust, breed fear' (official statement)

climate.label: Led Milwaukee County climate plan (~48% emissions cut, zero-carbon by 2050); wants state investment in solar and retrofits (campaign record)

education.label: Restore two-thirds state school funding, universal early childhood education; would not expand vouchers (Wisconsin Examiner voter guide)

safety.label: Mixed: says the state 'should not defund police' while investing in wraparound services and prevention (Wisconsin Examiner voter guide)

repro.label: 'Access to safe, legal abortion is essential healthcare'; co-sponsored 2017 resolution declaring abortion is health care (official statement)

democracy.label: Supports protecting voting rights and nonpartisan redistricting (campaign plan)

controversies.label: Ran a past Twitter account that posted crude, sexist and homophobic messages (he says he wasn't its sole author), and oversaw a county health-insurance lapse affecting employees, after which he fired the administrator (WPR)

nullNotes.taxes: checked Badger Basics plan, campaign Plan page (property-tax relief via local revenue reform, does not fit the axis), and Wisconsin Examiner voter guide, nothing documented

candidates.name: Tom Tiffany
candidates.background: U.S. Representative for Wisconsin's 7th District since 2020; before that a state senator, state representative, town supervisor, and river-excursion business co-owner. Won the Aug 11 Republican primary with about 95% of the vote; endorsed by President Trump and Vice President Vance.
priorities: Immigration enforcement; ban sanctuary cities statewide

cost.label: Freeze property taxes, drive down energy costs, cut regulations that raise housing/childcare/health costs (campaign site)

health.label: Backs price transparency and market competition; opposes Medicare for All (Fox6 primary coverage)

housing.label: Cut regulations to make housing more affordable (campaign site)

immigration.label: Ban sanctuary cities statewide, enforce immigration laws, secure the border; opposes amnesty (campaign site)

taxes.label: Property-tax freeze; repeal what he calls Evers' '400-year property tax increase'; touts federal tax cuts (campaign site)

climate.label: Promote baseload power, fight wind/solar projects on farmland; record of opposing environmental regulation (campaign site)

education.label: Focus on reading/writing/math, move money from administration to classrooms, opposes race-based curricula framing (campaign site)

safety.label: More resources for law enforcement; end 'revolving door' policies for repeat offenders (campaign site)

repro.label: Pro-life; supports Wisconsin's existing 20-week abortion ban, calling it a 'compromise'; voted to defund Planned Parenthood as a state legislator (Fox6)

democracy.label: Voted against certifying Arizona's and Pennsylvania's 2020 electoral votes; signed the Texas v. Pennsylvania amicus brief (Wikipedia)

controversies.label: Objected to certifying 2020 electoral votes and signed the Texas v. Pennsylvania brief; one of 14 House votes against the Juneteenth holiday (Wikipedia)

candidates.name: Derrick Van Orden
candidates.background: Derrick Van Orden is the incumbent U.S. Representative for Wisconsin's 3rd District and a retired Navy SEAL, described as a staunch supporter of President Trump. He won the seat in 2022 and held off Rebecca Cooke in 2024; the 2026 rematch is one of the Democrats' top House targets.

candidates.name: Rebecca Cooke
candidates.now: Small business owner and nonprofit founder
candidates.background: Rebecca Cooke was raised on an Eau Claire dairy farm, founded the Red Letter Grant nonprofit that funds women-owned startups, and still waits tables part time. Appointed by Gov. Evers to the Wisconsin Economic Development Corporation board, she narrowly lost to Van Orden in 2024 and won the August 11, 2026 primary with 60.4% over Emily Berge, endorsed by both Blue Dog Democrats and Bernie Sanders.
priorities: An economy built for working families
